elements.name: Parent User
elements.rationale: The code distinguishes parent users as a role and gives them dedicated registration, login, profile, child-management, and video-upload capabilities.

elements.name: Child User
elements.rationale: The code explicitly supports child logins and child-only behaviors such as approved-video access, requesting videos, and tracking watch/search history.

elements.name: Administrator
elements.rationale: The system has an admin role with separate authorization checks for listing users, changing roles, and deactivating accounts.

elements.name: Web Browser / Frontend Client
elements.rationale: A React frontend sends API requests to the backend and stores authentication state in browser localStorage.

elements.name: MongoDB Database
elements.rationale: The backend connects to MongoDB as an external database service used for application persistence.

elements.name: Authentication and Account Management Service
elements.rationale: This router handles registration, multiple login flows, current-user lookup, and password changes, using JWTs and the User/Child models.

elements.name: Authorization Middleware
elements.rationale: Dedicated middleware verifies bearer JWTs, loads the user record, and enforces role-based access before protected routes proceed.

elements.name: Child Profile and Activity Management Service
elements.rationale: This router manages child profiles, approvals, requests, and child search/watch history for parent and child flows.

elements.name: Video Management and Streaming Service
elements.rationale: This router uploads videos, lists/query videos, retrieves metadata, streams stored files, and processes likes/comments.

elements.name: User Administration and Profile Service
elements.rationale: This router updates user profiles, returns user statistics, and provides admin-only user management functions.

elements.name: Image Upload Handling
elements.rationale: A dedicated multer-based component validates image MIME/extensions and writes uploaded image files into an uploads/images directory.

elements.name: Static Upload File Serving
elements.rationale: The backend exposes the uploads directory over HTTP so stored images and videos can be retrieved by clients.

elements.name: User Accounts Store
elements.rationale: The User Mongoose model persists parent/admin account records including credentials, six-digit code, role, and profile image.

elements.name: Child Profiles Store
elements.rationale: The ChildProfile Mongoose model persists child identity details, parent linkage, approvals, requests, and search/watch history.

elements.name: Video Metadata Store
elements.rationale: The Video Mongoose model persists video metadata, uploader linkage, moderation state, engagement data, and file path references.

elements.name: Uploaded Media Files
elements.rationale: The system writes uploaded videos and images to server-side filesystem directories under uploads and uploads/images.

elements.name: Browser Local Storage
elements.rationale: The frontend persists authentication token, user object, and cookie-banner dismissal state in browser localStorage.

flows.description: Parent registration data from browser/client to authentication service, including username, email, password, firstName, lastName, sixDigitCode, and optional profileImage upload.
Uploaded parent profile image file passed from registration handling into image upload middleware for validation and storage.
Parent profile image file written to uploads/images on disk with generated filename.
New user account record written, containing username, email, password, firstName, lastName, sixDigitCode, and optional profileImage filename.
Existing user account lookup by email or username during registration to detect duplicates.
Child profiles associated with the new or logging-in parent are read to include childrenProfiles in authentication/profile responses.
Registration/login/profile responses returned to browser with JWT token and user object, including userType and childrenProfiles or children.
JWT token and authenticated user object stored in browser localStorage after register, parent login, child login, or legacy login.
Stored token and user data read from browser localStorage on app start to restore session state.
Bearer token from browser localStorage attached to Authorization header on API requests and supplied to authorization middleware.
Authorization middleware reads user account by decoded JWT userId and excludes password to validate token and active account.
Authenticated user context (user object plus JWT-derived userType) passed to protected authentication/account routes such as /me and change-password.
Login and account-management requests from browser/client to authentication service, including email/password, optional sixDigitCode, and password change data.
User account records read by email or id during login, parent login, child login, current-profile lookup, and password verification.
Updated user account data written when changing password; new password is saved and hashed by the model pre-save hook.
Child profile and child activity requests from browser/client, including child name, dateOfBirth, gender, optional idImage, videoId requests, search queries, and watch history data.
Child ID image upload passed from child profile create/update handlers into image upload middleware.
Child ID image file written to uploads/images on disk with generated filename.
Child profile records written or updated with name, dateOfBirth, gender, parent id, optional idImage, requests, approvals, searchHistory, watchHistory, and isActive status.
Child profile data read for parent child listings, single profile retrieval, approved videos, history views, request processing, and child activity tracking.
Video metadata read by child-profile service to validate requested videos, populate requested/approved video details, and enrich watch history.
Responses to browser/client containing child profiles, approved videos, searchHistory, watchHistory, and results of request/approval/delete operations.
Video API requests from browser/client, including upload multipart form data, browse filters, likes, comments, and video fetch/stream requests.
Uploaded video file written to uploads directory on disk and later read as a file stream for playback.
Video metadata written or updated, including title, description, filename, originalName, filePath, fileSize, uploader, category, ageRange, tags, likes, comments, views, and isActive.
Video metadata read for public feed, my-videos list, single video retrieval, metadata updates, delete, like/unlike, comments, and counts.
Video service responses to browser/client containing video metadata, public feed results, my-videos list, like/comment results, and streamed video content.
Uploaded media files stored on disk are read by static file serving middleware from the uploads directory.
Static uploaded files under /uploads, such as profile or child ID images, are served to the browser/client.
Browser/client requests to user profile and administration service for profile retrieval, profile updates, stats, admin user listing, role change, and deactivation.
User account updates written for profile changes, admin role updates, and account deactivation.
User account records read for profile retrieval, email uniqueness checks, stats/user administration queries, and admin listings without passwords.
Child profile records counted or read by user service for parent profile childrenProfiles and parent statistics.
Video metadata read by user service to compute parent statistics such as videoCount and totalViews.
User/profile/admin responses returned to browser/client containing user profile data, childrenProfiles, statistics, user lists, updated roles, or deactivated user records.
Authentication/account service connects to MongoDB and issues user/child database operations through Mongoose models.
flows.uncertainty_note: The code shows Mongoose connection and model operations; the direct network hop to MongoDB is mediated by Mongoose.

flows.description: Parent enters registration, login, profile, child-management, and video-upload data into the web browser/frontend client.
Child enters login credentials, searches, and video request/play actions into the web browser/frontend client.
Administrator uses the web browser/frontend client to initiate admin user-management requests such as listing users, changing roles, and deactivating accounts.
